newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay blue chips take a hit on political concerns.
newsitem.headline: Bombay blue chips take a hit on political concerns.

text.p: Share prices tumbled in delayed trade at the Bombay Stock Exchange on Monday, affected by news that a regional party plans to pull out of the United Front minority government, traders said.
But the market fall was only a nervous sell-off as the government faced no immediate threat, they said.

The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagan (DMK) party of Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said in a statement it planned to pull out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party government but would continue to provide support from the outside.

"It seems to be a sentimental, knee-jerk reaction," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at brokerage Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs, referring to the more than two percent fall in Bombay's benchmark index minutes after opening on Monday.
DMK leaders blamed the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), accusing it of interfering in Gujral's Janata Dal party.
The DMK accounts for less than a tenth the United Front's 178 seats in the 545-member lower house of parliament, and depends on make-or-break support from the Congress party, with 140 members.
Frontline stocks including Reliance Industries, State Bank of India (SBI) and Tata Iron & Steel Company (TISCO) bore the brunt of selling pressure, dealers said.
"There is no panic selling, but the speculative sell-off in major stocks has sent the market tumbling," said an equities dealer at a local institutional brokerage.

Among individual stocks, tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd tumbled 48.0 rupees to 495.50 after the federal government launched an enquiry into alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), traders said.
The Business Standard newspaper said on Monday ITC directors accused in the $110 million FERA violation case will not be asked to resign from the board.
The federal Enforcement Directorate is investigating the case. ITC is India's leading cigarette maker and is an affiliate of B.A.T. Industries Plc of U.K.
ITC shares ended 38.60 rupees down at 506.05 rupees at the National Stock Exchange ahead of the last day of end-account trade on the bourse.
The Bombay exchange will close at 1700 hours (1130 GMT) Monday in delayed trading hours.
